text:
alex_support: FYI — acme-inc reporting huge spike of 5xxs from our hosted inference API starting ~09:12 UTC. They see 500/502/504 across multiple endpoints (generation + embeddings). Customer says it started after ~09:10 and affects prod only. Sample curl + response: 

alex_support: ```bash
curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate\" \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-qa","input":"short prompt"}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
{\"error\":{\"message\":\"control-plane: routing policy lookup failed: 5xx\",\"code\":502,\"correlation_id\":\"c0rr-9a1-4b2\"}}
```

alex_support: Correlation IDs: c0rr-9a1-4b2, c0rr-9a1-4f7, c0rr-9a1-50a. Customer is on Dedicated? no, hosted. They're hitting ~30% error rate on ~200 req/s. Escalating to oncall. @maria_oncall can you triage? :rotating_light:

josh_cs: +1 prioritized. Account acme-inc, tier: pro, workspace id wks_acme_42. They're pretty sensitive to downtime. Please keep me in the loop, I'll handle comms.

maria_oncall: On it. First checks: control-plane service health (auth/session svc, routing-policy svc, config-db). Can someone grab the recent graphs from Grafana for: 
 - auth/session error rate
 - routing-policy latency (p50/p95)
 - configdb query error/latency

maria_oncall: Also please run a quick curl to the control-plane health endpoints so we know if a specific component is failing: 
```bash
curl -sS https://controlplane.internal/health | jq .
curl -sS https://routing-policy.internal/health | jq .
curl -sS https://auth.internal/health | jq .
```

devon_runtime: I can see routing-policy throwing 503s with \"context deadline exceeded\" around 09:10-09:20. Pasting log snippet: 

devon_runtime: ```
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z routing-policy service request_id=rp-4a2 err=\"context deadline exceeded\" path=/v1/lookup tenant=wks_acme_42
2026-03-15T09:12:07Z configdb query_id=q-8f3 duration=12034ms err=\"read timeout\" shard=shard-3
2026-03-15T09:12:08Z routing-policy service request_id=rp-4b9 upstream_err=\"configdb: read timeout\"\n```

devon_runtime: Looks like configdb read latencies spiked on shard-3 causing routing-policy to timeout, which then bubbles up to control-plane and results in 5xx to the API gateway.

alex_support: I captured a full HTTP trace from the customer with headers: 
```
X-Request-ID: c0rr-9a1-4b2
X-Gateway: apigw-7
X-Controlplane-Route: lookup/tenant/wks_acme_42
```

maria_oncall: Good find. If the routing-policy can't get a policy, the gateway currently fails closed (returns 502). Short-term mitigation options: 
 - enable cached-default-routing for gateway (fallback to cached policy)
 - increase routing-policy and configdb timeouts during surge
 - toggle feature flag to use static default policy for impacted tenants

maria_oncall: Can someone flip cached-default for acme workspace while we debug? Admin API below: 
```bash
POST https://admin.internal/v1/workspaces/wks_acme_42/flags 
{ "flags": { "use_cached_default_routing": true }}
```

devon_runtime: I'll flip the flag and also look at recent deploys. I see a routes service rollout at ~08:58 (tag v2026.03.15-routes). Not sure if it contributed, but configdb shards show increased hot reads. Quick mitigation: scale configdb read-replicas + restart routing-policy pods so they reconnect to replicas.

devon_runtime: Running: ```bash
kubectl -n controlplane rollout undo deploy/routes --to-revision=12  # rollback to pre-2026.03.15
kubectl -n controlplane scale sts configdb-read --replicas=5
```

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: rollback routes -> revision 12 by devon_runtime. Rollout status: 2/3 pods updated, 1 pending.

deploy-bot: scaling: statefulset configdb-read -> replicas=5. Starting new pods.

alex_support: Customer reports partial improvement: errors down to ~8% now. They still see occasional 500s.

maria_oncall: Keep an eye on p95 for routing-policy. Also check auth/session store — we saw a few session-store timeouts earlier, maybe due to the same configdb read pressure (session metadata stored in configdb). If session lookups fail, auth can also 5xx.

devon_runtime: Confirmed — session-store read errors matching same timestamps and shard. Log: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:10Z session-store request_id=sess-33 err=\"configdb read timeout\" shard=shard-3 duration=11890ms
```

maria_oncall: Ok mitigation plan: 
1) keep cached-default-routing enabled for impacted tenants (acme and a few others)
2) keep configdb-read replicas at 5 and monitor for stabilization
3) rollback routes rollout and keep it paused until we validate queries
4) add temporary alert for configdb shard latency > 3s (already paging)
5) longer term: add more aggressive query caching in routing-policy and move session-store metadata to a faster KV (redis) for hot tenants.

josh_cs: Drafting customer message: \"We've identified a transient spike in our control-plane config DB causing routing and session lookups to time out, which resulted in 5xx responses. We've applied a fallback routing and increased read capacity to stabilize traffic; we're monitoring and will follow up with a postmortem and timeline.\" Thoughts?

sara_prod: message is good. Add ETA for follow-up: we'll have a postmortem within 48 hours and a patch plan to reduce blast radius.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete: routes -> revision 12. All pods updated.

devon_runtime: Traffic looks healthy after rollback + scaling. p50/p95 routing-policy latency back to normal (p95 ~ 120ms). Error rate <1% across affected endpoints.

alex_support: Customer confirmed service recovered and thanked the team. Marking resolved on support ticket but we'll keep thread open until postmortem. :white_check_mark:

maria_oncall: Filing follow-up actions: 
 - PM/Eng to design caching and move session metadata to Redis (ticket INF-4532)
 - Improve shard-level alerts and autoscaling for configdb reads (INF-4533)
 - Add gateway fallback to cached policy for more tenants and telemetry (INF-4534)

maria_oncall: Thanks everyone. Closing triage — will assign owners for the follow-ups and add timelines. :v:
